correctness.rationale: Interpret the decoded RESULT.md mathematical statement with standard single-backslash TeX syntax (its public file is mistakenly double-escaped). For fixed mu>0 and alpha in [0,pi), let C_mu=cos(alpha)J_mu-sin(alpha)Y_mu and normalized Phi=1-C_{mu-1}C_{mu+1}/C_mu^2. At assigned source minimizer, exact identities b(1+zeta)=1 and a^2=(1+zeta)*(mu^2-zeta^2)/zeta imply the algebraic invariant a^2(1-b)+((1-b)/b)^2=mu^2. Since source b->1 and a->infinity, zeta=(1-b)/b=O(a^-2), so 1-b=mu^2/a^2+O(a^-6). Classical fixed-order cylinder zero law c_n=pi*n+O(1), with minimizer between c_n and c_{n+1}, implies a=pi*n+O(1) and 1-b=mu^2/(pi^2*n^2)+O(n^-3). The derivation is exact and not a finite sample. The source 2026 theorem with unique minima and qualitative convergence is a needed premise recorded in assigned file; fresh source full text could not be read independently due institutional connection. originality.rationale: The claim supplies a natural exact rate for the fresh sharp normalized cylinder nodal minima. Crucially, the highly relevant full 2016 Baricz-Ponnusamy-Singh primary Theorem 3 locates extrema of the UNNORMALIZED Turánian Delta=C_mu²-C_{mu-1}C_{mu+1} at zeros of adjacent-order functions. That is not the minimizer of the ratio Delta/C_mu² considered here, so not an implication-equivalent predecessor. Its Theorem 1 inequality provides qualitative lower bounds; DLMF zeros only index spacing. The fresh 2026 abstract reports monotonic convergence, no displayed rate; full 2026 primary inaccessible, so possible implicit extraction remains a residual risk.
